clue.text: It's difficult for monsters to eat apples here

indicators.note: to eat means the monsters take the next word inside themselves

parts.note: orcs are monsters of fantasy fiction
difficult means hard

explanation.surface: Ogres would struggle to feed on fruit in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to eat' is the container signal. The definition 'apples here' is a place where apples grow, and 'It's' and 'for' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit trees such as apple trees are grown together in plantations of this kind.

clue.text: Flag shows unusual gold parrot

indicators.note: unusual means the metal's letters appear in an odd order

parts.note: a lory is a small brightly coloured parrot

explanation.surface: A banner displays a rare golden bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges GOLD to OLDG.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname for the national banner of the United States.

clue.text: Not totally idyllic, a prime spot for tourists

indicators.note: not totally means only part of the run of words is used, a stretch inside them

explanation.surface: A place not quite perfect, yet a major holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not totally' points to a run of letters inside IDYLLIC A PRIME.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian island in the Bay of Naples, popular with holidaymakers.

clue.text: Worker, one to join old church in Turkish city

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An employee joins an ancient church in a city of Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient city, now Antakya, in southern Turkey, important in early Christianity.

clue.text: What could be at sea may be found in boatyard however

indicators.note: may be found in means the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A vessel could be located in a shipyard, though.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be found in' points to letters inside BOATYARD HOWEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab sailing vessel with a lateen sail is one craft that floats offshore.

clue.text: Ornament cleaner repeatedly knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over means the doubled cleaner is turned upside down, read backwards in the grid
repeatedly means the cleaner appears twice in a row

parts.note: a mop is a cleaner for floors

explanation.surface: A decorative piece keeps getting toppled by the cleaning staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives MOPMOP and 'knocked over' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A woolly ball sewn onto a hat as decoration is a type of trimming.

clue.text: Cheering something new inn brought out

indicators.note: brought out means the pub is removed from the longer word

parts.note: an innovation is something new
the word inn as written

explanation.surface: Applause greets a novel public house being unveiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought out' takes INN from the start of INNOVATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Applause and acclaim from an audience, as in a standing tribute.

clue.text: Academic errs with spoof being found out

indicators.note: being found out means the letters are exposed and laid out anew

explanation.surface: A scholar slips up and is exposed as a hoax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being found out' rearranges ERRS and SPOOF together.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior university teacher holding a chair is a top academic post.

clue.text: Very small home in quiet setting

indicators.note: setting means the quiet word forms a mount around the next piece, as a ring sets a gem

parts.note: mute means quiet
in means at home

explanation.surface: A tiny house in a tranquil location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' is the container signal, a mount holding a stone; 'in' just links. IN for 'home' is the crossword sense of being at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny or minuscule, pronounced with stress on the second syllable.

clue.text: Alternative to second e entry in encyclopedia?

definitions.text: Alternative to second e entry in encyclopedia?

parts.words: Alternative to second e entry in encyclopedia?
parts.note: the British spelling encyclopaedia puts the vowel pair a-e where the American spelling has a lone second e, and that vowel pair is the thing described

explanation.surface: A question about variant spellings in a reference work.
explanation.walkthrough: The British spelling 'encyclopaedia' uses AE where the American has the second E; the AE (often printed as a joined ligature) is a combined vowel sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A gliding combination of two vowel sounds in one syllable, like the ae printed as a ligature, is the phonetic term meant.

clue.text: What can make men edgy — a handsome boy

indicators.note: can make means these letters may be formed into something else

explanation.surface: Something that makes men nervous is a good-looking lad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' rearranges MEN EDGY and A. In Greek myth Zeus carried off the youth to be cupbearer.
explanation.definitionFit: The beautiful Trojan youth of Greek myth, carried off by Zeus to be cupbearer.

clue.text: A university lecturer given right to keep ornament

indicators.note: to keep means the lecturer holds the next letter inside

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A college tutor is permitted to retain a decorative item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to keep' puts R inside DON, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: To decorate or embellish something is the verb sense of ornament here.

clue.text: Provided help in west side of capital

indicators.note: in means the help sits inside the cut-down capital
west side of means only the left half of the capital is kept

parts.note: London is the UK capital
help means aid

explanation.surface: Assistance was given in the western part of the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'west side of' keeps the left half of the capital's name (the first three letters); 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay something on is an idiom for supplying or arranging it, as with food or transport.

clue.text: Very poor drunk ending it

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone destitute, drink finishing them off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges ENDING IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym for destitute or penniless, describing someone lacking basic means.

clue.text: Work against friend, one inflamed within

indicators.note: within means the next pieces go inside the friend

parts.note: mate means friend
I is the Roman numeral for one
lit means set alight, inflamed

explanation.surface: Oppose a pal who has a burning anger inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' is the container signal; 'inflamed' is the past tense of setting alight, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: To be a strong factor opposing something, usually followed by against.

clue.text: Good chaps who seem to be very hard when lacking polish?

definitions.text: Good chaps who seem to be very hard when lacking polish?

parts.words: Good chaps who seem to be very hard when lacking polish?
parts.note: reads as kind men with gruff manners, and also as uncut gems, the hardest stones, before they are polished

explanation.surface: Kind-hearted fellows with a tough, unrefined exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncut gemstones are very hard and unpolished; the phrase also means people who are good at heart but rough in manner.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for decent people whose manners are coarse, drawn from uncut gemstones.

clue.text: Strange things in nature the man had discovered

indicators.note: strange things in means odd changes happen to the letters of the following word

parts.note: the man had is he'd, written HED

explanation.surface: Odd natural phenomena the fellow had dug up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange things in' is the anagram signal on 'nature'; 'the man had' contracts to he'd, the apostrophe dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Dug up or brought to light, as an archaeologist finds a relic.

clue.text: See Doris eat quirkily to get a heavenly body

indicators.note: quirkily means the letters are rearranged in an odd way

explanation.surface: Watch a woman eating in an odd manner to get a celestial object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quirkily' rearranges DORIS EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rocky object orbiting the Sun is a minor planet in space.

clue.text: Dire prospects destroyed team's feeling of loyalty

indicators.note: destroyed means the two words are smashed and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: Grim outlook has wrecked a squad's morale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges DIRE PROSPECTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase for the shared pride and solidarity of members of a group.

clue.text: Writer, a woman

parts.note: reads as a female author, specifically one who writes verse

explanation.surface: A female author.
explanation.walkthrough: A writer who is a woman, and specifically one writing verse; the term is now dated.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated term for a female composer of verse.

clue.text: When drunk, I re-echo toast

indicators.note: when drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Under the influence, I repeat a drinking salute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When drunk' rearranges I RE-ECHO.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheery word said when raising glasses, also a casual goodbye.

clue.text: Men losing head and heart shout at a concert

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: core means heart

explanation.surface: Men without a leader and soul cry out at a gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops the M of MEN to leave EN.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience's call for an extra performance once the show ends.

clue.text: Poisonous vapour dispersed by avengers

indicators.note: dispersed means the letters are scattered and regathered

explanation.surface: Avenging heroes scatter a toxic cloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersed' rearranges AVENGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical weapon that attacks the nervous system is a lethal toxic agent.

clue.text: Hunting dog brings black bird

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an eagle is a bird

explanation.surface: A hound fetches a dark-feathered bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small scent hound bred for chasing hares is one breed of hunting hound.

clue.text: Sort to give info to America

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Kind enough to pass details to the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is informal British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind or class, especially a taxonomic rank above species.

clue.text: Bridge taking one out of country

indicators.note: out of means the numeral is taken from the country

parts.note: Spain is a country
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A crossing removes someone from a nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... out of' removes I from SPAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend across, as a crossing over a river does.

clue.text: Old church with mostly red pigment

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the colour word is dropped

parts.note: the colour red written out

explanation.surface: An ancient chapel mostly painted in a reddish shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of RED to leave RE.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthy yellow-brown colouring made from clay is a natural paint material.

clue.text: Ten operas translated into universal language

indicators.note: translated means the letters are converted into a new form

explanation.surface: Ten operatic works rendered into an international tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'translated' rearranges TEN OPERAS.
explanation.definitionFit: An invented auxiliary tongue devised by Zamenhof for worldwide use.

clue.text: Most ancient parts of Leeds crumbling with time

indicators.note: crumbling means the city name falls apart into a new order

explanation.surface: Bits of a Yorkshire city decaying over the years are the oldest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumbling' is the anagram signal; 'parts of' is a linking phrase. Leeds is a city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Oldest, used especially of the first-born among siblings.

clue.text: Supported conclusion to restrict inadequate county

indicators.note: to restrict means the conclusion closes round the shortened county

parts.note: conclusion means end

indicators.note: inadequate means the county falls short by its final letter

parts.note: Dorset is a county in south-west England

explanation.surface: Backed a final limit on an underperforming shire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inadequate' drops the county's final letter; 'to restrict' is the container signal. Dorset is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Backed or approved, as when a candidate receives public backing.
